decisions.note: Every <Link viewTransition> in src/views does nothing: React Router only honours the prop under a data router, and src/App.tsx mounts <BrowserRouter> + <Routes>. Verified by patching document.startViewTransition and clicking a product card — it was never called. So the product-image continuity the SPEC asks for has never run, and the only transition that does fire is withDirectionalTransition() on a filter chip, which slides and scales the whole page (1.06 → 1) on a spring that overshoots — the jerky zoom the team reported. The lab studies drive the transition explicitly (src/lab/subpages/shared.tsx › ContinuityLink) and name only the clicked image, so exactly one pair morphs. Whichever directions are chosen, the fix belongs in src/views too.
decisions.outcome: Fixed. src/App.tsx declares a real route table under createBrowserRouter instead of <BrowserRouter> + a descendant <Routes>. Measured before and after on the running site: a product-card click started 0 view transitions and now starts 1, and the back navigation replays it. A splat route with <Routes> underneath was tried first and does NOT work — a descendant <Routes> matches below the data router, so the Link's prop never reaches the router that would honour it. The other half of the note is also gone: withDirectionalTransition no longer fires on a filter chip, because motion proposal 05 landed in the same pass.

decisions.note: Team 09/09: “hiện tại cái arc đang chỉ vào hư vô”. All three draw the SAME curve at the same thickness in the same place, so the only variable is motion. The band is a stroke rather than a filled shape: thickness stays exactly constant through every turn, and it is what makes option 1 possible at all. DECIDED: C · Sóng biển, shipped in src/components/HeroWave.tsx. The team took the ambient option over the one-shot; the recommendation for 1 · Nét bút stands recorded above as what was argued, not as what was chosen. Both ends are pinned to the white plate's foot at 75.4% of the hero — an extra requirement that arrived with the choice, and one the bell-shaped amplitude makes possible because the ends are the quiet part of this motion. The three studies stay in /lab/hero-wave.

decisions.recommendation: 1 · NÉT BÚT. The hero already has three moving things on it — the deck's carousel, the ribbon's blink, and the marquee below the fold — and BrandSurround's own header argues that the deck is the moving thing on this screen. A band that never stops is a fourth. Drawing itself in once says everything a wave has to say and then gets out of the way, and it is the only option that costs nothing for the rest of the visit. If the team wants the hero to feel alive at rest, 3 · SÓNG BIỂN is the one to take, not 2 — it does not fight the ribbon loop.

decisions.question: What is a collection for — a cut of the catalogue, or an argument about a group of objects? And does it get pages of its own?
decisions.note: Team 09/09: "Chỉ hiển thị collections ở homepage sẽ gây giới hạn số lượng sản phẩm có thể có cho 1 collection (cùng lắm là 10 sản phẩm)", and asked for two families — Catalogue and Curation — with three directions each. The homepage strip holds eight tiles, so a collection is currently not a thing with a size but a thing that fits in a strip: an editor cannot put twenty pieces in one, write about it, or link to it. The five lab collections hold 11–22 products each, which is the point made in numbers.

decisions.recommendation: A1 as the floor, B2 as the layer on top. A1 is the only direction that answers the note directly — a collection gets a size of its own instead of one that fits in a strip — and it reuses the filter bar, the paging and the product card that /products already has, so it costs close to nothing. B2 sits on A1 without replacing it: add a cover screen and forty words to the top of A1's collection page and A1 becomes B2. A collection with copy gets the poster; one without is still a decent catalogue page rather than a broken article, which is the failure mode B1 and B3 both have.
decisions.openAfter: A3 is worth doing whichever family wins: ?collection= in the /products filter bar is a few lines and it buys "Mực và giấy dưới 300k", which no other direction can express. It does not replace the page, because a facet has no cover. Also unresolved: who writes the copy, and whether collections are seeded by hand or cut from the taxonomy — the lab cuts them from the taxonomy only so the drafts have realistic sizes.
